articles.descriptionJa: キックオフに向けて発表された最新のレポートや公式発表に基づく、更新された欠場者情報と分析。
articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 2 Buzz 

Week 2 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 2

Biggest concerns heading into Week 2

Players with early starts

Joe Burrow, QB, Bengals (back): Burrow is dealing with back soreness and is listed as questionable but is expected to start. The quarterback stated that it would be "ridiculous" if the injury caused him to miss Week 2. Even in a tough matchup like the Texans, Burrow is a fantasy QB1.

If you want to avoid the matchup, Jaxson Dart and Brock Purdy are realistic options that a fantasy manager could have backing up Burrow. If you're skittish, those two could be started over him. However, for most of you, the choice should be to ride with Burrow.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): After missing the Patriots' opener because of an ankle injury, Henderson returned to practice this week and says he is "ready to go" for Week 2. Henderson will share work in the backfield with Rhamondre Stevenson. However, he is the more explosive option and therefore brings more fantasy upside.

Henderson can be played over Quinshon Judkins, MarShawn Lloyd, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, Rico Dowdle, Blake Corum, Kenny Gainwell and Jonathon Brooks.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After a huge Week 1 performance, Coker was limited in practice to start the week because of an ankle injury. He was able to log a full practice Friday and was removed from the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 2. While the Panthers will not often have "scorefests" like they did in Week 1, Coker's usage jumps off the screen. He saw nine targets -- three of the deep variety -- and finished with 138 yards and a touchdown, while narrowly missing a second score.

Coker is a high upside WR3. You can feel comfortable playing him over DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr, Alec Pierce, Marvin Harrison Jr and Chris Godwin Jr.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (knee): Kamara has "moved well" at practice and Kellen Moore has said he should play this week. He is a flex option that brings some PPR upside, but also some risk as we do not know how much work he will see. If he plays, it would be a bit of a thorn in the side of Travis Etienne Jr., who saw nine targets in Week 1.

articles.headline: Ravens' Zay Flowers downgraded to out because of hamstring injury
articles.description: The Baltimore Ravens downgraded Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers to out for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズのゼイ・フラワーズ、ハムストリング負傷で欠場へダウングレード
articles.descriptionJa: ボルティモア・レイブンズは、日曜日のニューオーリンズ・セインツ戦に向けて、プロボウル選出のワイドレシーバー、ゼイ・フラワーズのステータスを欠場（out）にダウングレードしました。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- The Baltimore Ravens downgraded Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers to out for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, leaving quarterback Lamar Jackson without one of his most valuable playmakers.

Flowers, the Ravens' No. 1 receiver, aggravated his left hamstring injury in Sunday's season-opening 41-23 win at the Indianapolis Colts. He missed the first two practices of the week before being a limited participant Friday.

The Ravens had listed Flowers as doubtful Friday before officially scratching him Saturday. This is the fourth game that Flowers will miss in his four-year career and his first since the 2024 AFC divisional playoff game at Buffalo.

The loss of Flowers is significant for Jackson and Baltimore. Over the past 18 games, Flowers has 91 catches for 1,361 yards. During that same stretch, the Ravens' other wide receivers have combined for 55 catches for 814 yards.

With Flowers ruled out and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve, the Ravens will be without two of their top three wide receivers.

Rashod Bateman now becomes the receiver with the most familiarity with Jackson. The other four healthy wide receivers are LaJohntay Wester, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and Chris Moore.

Earlier in the week, Ravens coach Jesse Minter said his advice to the healthy receivers is "run at the opportunity."

"I think the first game was a great example that the ball can really go anywhere in our offense," Minter said. "Just being very precise, being very detailed, being in the right spot, the ball can find you. Playing fast and playing with confidence, we have a lot of confidence in all those guys."

In addition to downgrading Flowers, the Ravens placed top backup cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) on injured reserve and signed practice squad linebacker Carl Jones to the 53-man roster.

Baltimore elevated offensive tackle Gerad Lichtenhan from the practice squad. The addition of an extra offensive tackle could indicate that left tackle Ronnie Stanley (questionable, toe) might not play.

Stanley has been sidelined for 45 games in his 10 seasons, but only one of those games was within the past two seasons. If he can't play, Carson Vinson could get his first career start.

articles.headline: Frank Lampard values Coventry's hard work after first Premier League win in 25 years
articles.description: Frank Lampard said he was grateful for his team's work ethic after Coventry ended a four-game losing streak to claim their first Premier League win for 25 years.
articles.headlineJa: 25年ぶりのプレミアリーグ勝利後、フランク・ランパードがコヴェントリーのハードワークを評価
articles.descriptionJa: コヴェントリーが4連敗を止めて25年ぶりのプレミアリーグ勝利を飾った後、フランク・ランパードはチームのひたむきな姿勢に感謝を述べた。
articles.body:
Frank Lampard said he was grateful for his team's work ethic after Coventry ended a four-game losing streak to claim their first Premier League win for 25 years.

Jay Dasilva's second-half strike was enough for a 1-0 victory at Nottingham Forest after Igor Jesus' late equaliser was controversially ruled out by VAR.

"Having lost our first four games, all in different circumstances, I think it's easy to to feel negative, to feel like 'Where's the goal, where's the win coming from?'" Lampard told Sky Sports.

"And the reality is in football you have to fight for it, you have to work for it, you have to have organisation. I could go through so many players today, how they individually work within the collective.

"You make your own luck in terms of VAR. I think it is a foul, but I think when you work that hard, the boys deserve it."

Unlike fellow newly-promoted side Ipswich Town, Coventry's squad is short on top-flight experience -- only three of Saturday's starting lineup had played a Premier League before this season.

"We're a team with a lot of players that have come in and are playing their first stint of Premier League football, and I think it's human nature," Lampard said.

"You can't expect them to come in ... Not everyone's a Wayne Rooney or these superstars who just own it.

"You know, they've worked hard in their careers to get here. We're trying to get that out of them, and I think when they play like they did today, you can see that."

Coventry host Newcastle in their next game, after the three-week international break.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグVAR検証：ライスはブライトン戦で退場を免れて幸運だったのか？
articles.descriptionJa: VARはしばしば物議を醸しますが、判定はどのように下されているのでしょうか？専属審判のアンディ・デイヴィスが詳しく解説します。
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Was Rice lucky not to be sent off at Brighton?

Brighton & Hove Albion 3-0 Arsenal (Sept. 19)

Referee: Darren England

VAR: Tim Wood

Time: 90 + 7 mins

Incident: Possible red card for Arsenal's Declan Rice

What happened: Rice picked up a late yellow card when he appeared to kick out at Brighton's Malick Yalcouyé in an off-the-ball incident.

VAR decision: The on-field decision of yellow card was checked and cleared as correct by the VAR.

In these types of situations, VAR involvement can be triggered only if they believe the on-field refereeing team missed a violent act or an act or brutality. VAR was comfortable that the action by Rice did not meet either threshold, so the check was a straightforward one.

Verdict: This frustrated act by Rice was picked up in real time by the fourth official and certainly high risk, when considering many off-the-ball, non-footballing offenses are often interpreted as a red card offense by referees and matched by the expectations of football, so Rice can consider himself fortunate. However, I am comfortable that this action in isolation was a frustrated and petulant attempt at a trip on Yalcouyé and not a violent act or act of brutality, therefore a yellow card feels like a correct and sensible outcome.

VAR would never get involved in this situation unless there was clear evidence that the on-field outcome was incorrect, so the yellow card was correctly checked and cleared. Rice is very fortunate that the original on-field interpretation of his action was only a yellow card, otherwise he would be serving a three-game ban following the international break.

Why was Phil Foden sent off? And why was Enzo Fernández not ruled offside in Manchester derby?

Manchester United 0-1 Manchester City (Sept. 13)

What happened: City's Foden appeared to kick out at United's Bruno Fernandes following an untidy tangle between the two players.

articles.headline: NFL changes rules governing videoboard displays during kicks
articles.description: The NFL has modified what can be shown on videoboards during field goal and extra point attempts, an alteration coming in the wake of a viral social media post from a former analytics coach.
articles.headlineJa: NFL、キック時の大型映像装置の表示ルールを変更
articles.descriptionJa: NFLは、フィールドゴールおよびポイント・アフター・タッチダウンの試行中に大型映像装置に表示できる内容を変更しました。このルール変更は、元アナリティクスコーチによるSNSでの拡散投稿を受けて行われました。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The NFL recently informed teams that the league has modified what can be shown on videoboards during field goal and extra point attempts, an alteration coming in the wake of a viral social media post from a former analytics coach.

The NFL has long required all videoboards and ribbon boards to display a static image -- no flashing images, blinking effects, moving text/images etc. -- or an All-22 view, such as the high-sideline or high-end-zone angle, during kicks.

What has now changed, according to a memo obtained by ESPN that was sent to all clubs Sept. 7, is that teams must use the same All-22 angle or static image for both kicking teams. The modification is designed to ensure competitive equity. Teams were warned that violations will result in discipline.

Ryan Paganetti, a former analytics coach with the Philadelphia Eagles, Jacksonville Jaguars and Las Vegas Raiders, posted on X that he had studied a decade of New England Patriots television broadcasts when Bill Belichick was head coach from 2000 to 2023.

Paganetti's Sept. 1 social media post said he discovered that when opposing kickers prepared for an attempt, the videoboard displayed a reverse All-22 view of the kick. The result was a second set of offset goalposts shown on the videoboard, creating an optical illusion for opposing kickers.

Paganetti added that of the 52 kicks he studied that were attempted by the Patriots, the reverse All-22 view of the kick was never shown on the videoboard. Paganetti's post on X had nearly 17 million views as of this weekend.

The Patriots were operating within the rules during that time, according to the NFL. Other teams with videoboards behind uprights were experimenting with various things that were also within the rules.

But now that the league is requiring clubs to use the same All-22 angle or static image for both kicking teams, that practice would no longer be allowed.
